title: Core localization polynomial equivalence
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, f : Fin r → A, and i : Fin r. Write I = (∑ j, f(j)X_j - 1), B = A[X_j : j : Fin r]/I [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], Af = A localized at f(i), and Bf = B localized at the image of f(i) [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Equip Bf with its induced Af-algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property]. Then there exists an Af-algebra equivalence Af[Y_j : j ≠ i] ≃ Bf whose forward homomorphism is evaluation at the localized classes x_j of X_j, and whose inverse sends x_j to Y_j for every j ≠ i.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve): 'B_{f_i} is smooth over A_{f_i}. Details omitted.' (the isomorphism is the omitted detail)

proof.text: Use polynomial evaluation for the forward map. For the inverse, send X_i to f(i)⁻¹(1−∑ j ≠ i f(j)Y_j) and X_j to Y_j otherwise. The relation evaluates to zero; factor through the quotient, then extend through localization since f(i) maps to a unit. The extension respects Af coefficients by uniqueness of localization. The two composites fix all generators, using the relation for X_i, and are identities by polynomial, quotient and localization uniqueness.
